verdicts.claim: “Anthem — a live-set staple and enduring fan favourite that still defines his early sound” breaks the site's live-claim rule because of “still”
verdicts.evidence: The rule the finding invokes is tests/liveClaims.test.ts. Its ONGOING regex (lines 52-68) is a vocabulary of MOVEMENT attached to a FIGURE and a read date: "still (climbing|rising|growing|counting|going)", "and counting", "unbroken since", plus Spanish equivalents; the file's header says it checks 'the claim about currency … against a DATE — the day the figure last moved'. "still defines his early sound" (app/data/songs.ts line 95) does not match ONGOING, carries no figure, no date and no chart or streaming run that can stop moving; there is no site rule treating the bare word 'still' as a live claim, and the guard is green with this label in place. It is a qualitative characterisation, not a stat, so it cannot rot the way the Spotify-peak and Apple-run sentences did. The proposed rewording would also introduce a new typed factual claim ('a live-set staple since 2018') with no source behind it, which is worse than the wording it replaces.
verdicts.correctedFix: No change required. If Paul wants the sentence tightened as a matter of style, drop 'that still defines his early sound' rather than adding 'since 2018'; do not add it to any guard.

It is true that the numbers grid has no per-figure source or date (the charts and certs sections on the same page do carry a styles.source line), but the premise "the site's rule is that every figure is dated" is not what the site's own guard says: tests/publishedFigureStamps.test.tsx targets HAND-COUNTED headline figures with no date, and app/records/by-the-numbers/page.tsx lines 56–57 state the convention explicitly — "Every other figure on this page is either bot-refreshed or derived from a dated dataset, and the page's own 'Updated {asOf}' stamp covers them." The flagship /dai-dai page prints its bot-refreshed "1.09B" and "450M" cards the same way, with no per-figure date. The page is therefore not wrong, stale or broken, and it follows the site's existing convention for bot-refreshed figures; the proposed change is a site-wide design decision (it would also need a bot-written streamsAsOf field) rather than a page defect. Marked refuted as a defect; a one-line source note under the grid would be a reasonable enhancement for Paul to choose.

Repo (main @ 58b2df96): app/data/certifications.ts line 242 release row carries { c: "NZ", level: "Gold" }; certHistory rows for City Boys are only CA 2026 (line 582), UK Gold 2025 (622), FR Platinum 2025 (627), US Gold 2025 (638), FR Gold 2024 (663), UK Silver 2024 (664) — no NZ row in any year, and certHistory has zero NZ rows dated 2024 at all, while it holds NZ rows for 2022 (lines 704–705, 'RMNZ 2022-12-08/2022-09-08'), 2023, 2025 and 2026, so 13 Jun 2024 is inside the log's window and the 'awarded before the log started' exemption in tests/certs.test.ts (lines 240–262) does not apply. tsx count: certHistory 2024 = 20, intlCertHistory 2024 = 20; app/certifications/page.tsx line 212 renders CertHistoryByYear from intlCertHistory, so the page prints 20 and tests/certs.test.ts line 121 pins toBe(20). Trial-applied the fix locally (row + test bump): full vitest run 108 files / 1083 tests green, exit 0; then reverted.
verdicts.correctedFix: The proposed fix is correct and complete. (1) app/data/certifications.ts: insert after line 664 (`{ title: "City Boys", country: "UK", level: "Silver", year: 2024 },`) the row `{ title: "City Boys", country: "NZ", level: "Gold", year: 2024 }, // RMNZ 2024-06-13`. (2) tests/certs.test.ts lines 120–121: rename the case to "2024 has the published count of 21 certifications" and `toBe(20)` → `toBe(21)` with a dated comment (20 → 21 on 17 Sep 2026: City Boys NZ Gold, RMNZ via RadioScope 2024-06-13, on the release row since the snapshot but never logged). (3) app/data/certifications.ts line 852: CERTS_VERIFIED_ON "2026-09-16" → "2026-09-17" (the file's own rule: bump on every body read in the same edit as the row it changes). (4) app/data/updates.ts: new entry at the top of the array (line 48), date 2026-09-17, category Certifications, href /certifications, past tense, under 300 chars, e.g. “City Boys” has been Gold in New Zealand since 13 June 2024 — RMNZ's register dates the award; the plaque was already on the song's row, the dated log now carries the 2024 event. Only tests/certs.test.ts pins the figure (grep of tests/ for the 2024 count finds nothing in handoffTotals, publishedFigureStamps, searchIndex, certUnits); /records/visualized derives its bars from intlCertHistory and moves on its own; bestIntlYearBefore(2026) is unaffected (2023 = 44 stays the best prior year). Aside for the fixer: docs/sourcing/results/burna-raw.json row [147] records City Boys NZ as 'absent' from a read of aotearoamusiccharts.co.nz — that was the wrong body; RMNZ's register at RadioScope holds the row.

verdicts.claim: 119M YouTube views for the official video / 289M Spotify streams
verdicts.evidence: Bodies read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hLDQ88vAhIs (title 'Burna Boy - City Boys [Official Music Video]', ownerChannelName 'Burna Boy', publishDate 2023-09-22) embeds "viewCount":"118547647"; kworb.net/spotify/artist/3wcj11K77LjEY1PkEazffa_songs.html ('Last updated: 2026/09/16') row ['City Boys', '288,945,461', '136,422']. So the raw values are as the audit says, and the page's 119M / 289M (app/data/songs.ts lines 180 and 184, bot-written) are their nearest-million renderings. But nearest rounding is the site's tested convention for EVERY format, not a defect: tests/statsMonitor.test.ts line 92 pins formatStat(56517687, "M2") → "56.52M" (a floor would give 56.51M), line 416 pins 1,763,714,000 B3 → "1.764B" (floor: 1.763B), line 93 pins 747,000,000 M0 → "747M"; scripts/stats-lib.mjs formatStat (lines 423–449) rounds in every branch, and the same convention prints Dai Dai's 1.09B, the 17.81M Spotify followers and every M1/M2/B3 figure on the site. No 'never-inflated' rule exists anywhere in the repo: grep for inflat/round/nearest across app/methodology, app/about, app/faq, docs/*.md and the three earlier batch verdict files finds no such policy, and scripts/watched-metrics.json's $comment on both City Boys metrics concerns monotonicity (kind 'peak'), not rounding. Flooring only M0/compact would make song cards floor while every other stat rounds; flooring everything is a site-wide policy change that moves many published figures and tests. 119M is the correct nearest-million display of 118,547,647; the finding is a preference, not an error.
verdicts.correctedFix: No change to the page or to scripts/stats-lib.mjs. If Paul wants floor semantics it is a site-wide decision (formatStat for M0/M1/M2/B3/compact, tests/statsMonitor.test.ts lines 92–93 and 416–417, and every bot-written figure re-rendered), to be taken as a decision, not as a City Boys fix. One harmless comment nit for whoever next edits app/data/songs.ts: line 25–27's field comment still says ytViews is read from 'kworb per-video counts', while watched-metrics.json moved the source to the video's own YouTube page on 28 Aug 2026.

verdicts.claim: Typed prose figures duplicate derived data with no guard: "reached No. 2 in Nigeria, charted in eight countries and went 4× Platinum at home", "plus Platinum in Canada & France", FAQ and meta description
verdicts.evidence: Note-class finding; confirmed because the typed copy and the derived figure genuinely can diverge and nothing guards them. Data today (main @ 58b2df96): app/data/charts.ts line 349–352 City Boys entries NG 2, NL 14, UK 14, CH 24, FR 27, IE 44, SE 58, CA 70, GLB 143 — app/music/[song]/page.tsx line 29 derives countryEntries excluding GLB/GLBX = 8, bestPeak = 2; app/data/certifications.ts line 242–245: NG Platinum x4, CA Platinum, FR Platinum, UK Gold, US Gold, NZ Gold. The typed strings in app/data/songs.ts lines 187 (blurb), 189–190 (extraFacts), 200 (FAQ) and 205 (metaDescription) all say eight / No. 2 / 4× Platinum / Platinum in Canada and France, so they agree now, and I verified the underlying values at the bodies rather than only against the repo: TurnTable's archive (turntablecharts.com/api/ttc-proxy/api/chart/1/{week}/2023, Referer turntablecharts.com, base64 payload) walked from week 34/2023 to week 15/2024 — City Boys debuts at rank 3 in the 31 Aug 2023 issue, rank 2 / highestPosition 2 in the 7 Sep 2023 'Official Nigeria Top 100' issue, never higher in any later issue, so the all-time peak is 2; TCSN's page data (turntablecharts.com/certification, __NEXT_DATA__) holds {id 48, milestone 'Platinum_4', title 'City Boys', artiste 'Burna Boy', certifiedDate 2026-02-06}; Music Canada and SNEP Platine rows quoted under the next finding. Guard status: tests/songFacts.test.ts (lines 26–48) only checks that a fact enumerating Platinum countries names all of them; tests/songs.test.ts checks slugs, substance, SEO fields, no figures. The song page is one responsive component (app/music/[song]/page.tsx; no separate Mobile component), so both layouts read the same typed strings. The failure mode already happened once on this file ('On the Low' naming three of four Platinum countries, per the songFacts header). I also ran the proposed guard's logic across all 14 songs: last-last 14 typed vs 14 derived, wgft 12/12, city-boys 8/8 (three mentions) with NG 2 and 4×, jerusalema 16/16, alone 8/8, last-last 5× — every current mention agrees, so the guard would land green.
verdicts.correctedFix: The fix's direction is right; prefer the guard over deriving prose (the sentences are editorial and the OG image already derives its own numbers). Add a second `it` to tests/songFacts.test.ts after line 48: for each song, take blurb, metaDescription, every extraFacts `${v} ${l}` and every faqs[].a; map number words one…twenty to integers; assert every match of /(?:charted|charting) in (\w+) (?:countries|territories)/ equals the count of allChartItems entries with c not in {GLB, GLBX}; every /No\. (\d+) in Nigeria/ equals the NG entry's peak; every /(\d+)× Platinum (?:in Nigeria|at home)/ equals the NG cert's x in allItems. Import allChartItems from ../app/data/charts alongside the existing imports (lines 2–3). No data file changes; no other test pins these strings (tests/searchIndex only indexes titles/routes).

verdicts.claim: All six City Boys certifications are logged in the sourcing worklist as "pending" (never read at the body)
verdicts.evidence: Half true, and the half that matters is false. docs/sourcing/burna-boy.worklist.json (generated 2026-08-27, 231 rows) does hold City Boys|NG/CA/FR/UK/US/NZ at status 'pending' — but so are 230 of its 231 rows (only My Oasis|UK is 'confirmed'); docs/sourcing/PROGRESS.md line 40 lists writing the sweep's output back into that file as an open to-do. The rows were NOT 'never read at the body': docs/sourcing/results/burna-raw.json already carries body quotes from the Aug–Sep sweep — [5] TCSN '4xPLATINUM | City Boys | Burna Boy | Single | Feb 6, 2026'; [72] BPI '…Latest Certification: 07.03.2025'; [100] Music Canada 'January 28, 2026 | Platinum Single | Burna Boy — City Boys | Atlantic Records'; [125]/[130] SNEP Platine 22/05/2025 and Or 04/01/2024; [181] RIAA 'October 29, 2025 … earned RIAA Gold Award for CITY BOYS'. I re-read all six bodies on 17 Sep 2026 and they match the page and the audit's quotes: BPI certified-awards.bpi.co.uk/format/2/artist/4398/title/8340 'BURNA BOY CITY BOYS Most Recent Certification Gold … 07 March 2025 Gold 05 January 2024 Silver'; RIAA search ar=Burna+Boy&ti=City+Boys 'BURNA BOY CITY BOYS ON A SPACESHIP / BAD HABIT / ATLANTIC RECORDS SINGLE October 29, 2025', data-share-desc 'earned RIAA Gold Award for CITY BOYS'; Music Canada ?_gp_search=city+boys 'January 28, 2026 Platinum Single Burna Boy City Boys Atlantic Records'; SNEP ?interprete=Burna+Boy&titre=City+Boys 'CITY BOYS BURNA BOY … Platine Date de constat 22/05/2025' and 'Or Date de constat 04/01/2024'; TCSN __NEXT_DATA__ {id 48, Platinum_4, City Boys, Burna Boy, certifiedDate 2026-02-06}; RMNZ/RadioScope ['Burna Boy','City Boys','Gold','2024-06-13']. Nothing on /music/city-boys is wrong, stale or broken, and the finding proposes no change to app/data — it is docs housekeeping on a file that is uniformly unwritten. The CERTS_VERIFIED_ON bump it asks for belongs with finding 1 instead, because the file's own rule (certifications.ts lines 849–851) ties the bump to the edit that changes a row.
verdicts.correctedFix: No page fix. If the fixer wants the housekeeping anyway, it is harmless: set the six City Boys rows in docs/sourcing/burna-boy.worklist.json to status 'confirmed' with the URLs and verbatim quotes above and readOn '2026-09-17' — and correct docs/sourcing/results/burna-raw.json row [147], whose 'absent' NZ verdict came from aotearoamusiccharts.co.nz rather than RMNZ's register at RadioScope. Bump CERTS_VERIFIED_ON (certifications.ts line 852) once, in the finding-1 edit, not separately. No test reads the worklist (grep of tests/ and scripts/ for 'worklist' finds nothing).
